_comment: All galaxy map data. Field IDs verified against the orion2re Galaxy Map field dump (24 fields) in dev:doc/ext_api_dokumentation_v3.md — with one correction from a live screenshot: field 14 (hotkey R) is the RACES button, not Research; the dump's label was a guess. Research is opened via the sidebar in the original. Layout mirrors the original: stardate tops the sidebar column, TURN sits bottom-right (the former status_bar cutout).

frame._note: No frame image since decision 71 (work order 169; the cockpit frame and tools/frame_holes.py's boxes were removed by work order 189). The screen is the HUD layout: the map's floor in map_area, the title plate (also the GAME button) drawn in code by hudview.title_rect/render_title, the info panel and the nav bar. `title` here is the plate's word; `title_rect` is kept for reference only — the click area is hudview.title_rect.
frame.title: Game
frame._title_note: The original's top bar reads GAME and the bar itself is the game menu button (field 6, hotkey G). Kept literal rather than naming the screen.

game_menu_field._source: MAINSCR: _game_button = Add_Button_Field_(249, 5, ..., "G", 0x29) (mainscr.cpp:1389); type 0 and the end corner (307, 21) off the live list (the map dump in dev:doc/ext_api_dokumentation_v3.md). Looked up in the LIVE list by type and rect (decision 20), as the bottom bar's buttons are since work order 243: orion2re v2 puts five more hot keys before them, so the old index 6 is another field there.

zoom_out_field._source: MAINSCR: _zoom_out_button = Add_Button_Field_(244, 455, ..., "-") (mainscr.cpp:1381, :1392); type 0 and the end corner (298, 473) read off the live list, 17 September 2026 (work order 128 C) and in dev:tools/galaxy_box_fields.json. Parking looks this field up in the live list together with map_cancel's grid field and sends to the index it finds there; a list without both is not the galaxy map's, whatever screen number the game reports (the turn-start research prompt reports 0 and its field 9 is a choice row).

map_cancel._transcribed: TRANSCRIBED: a right click on the map. The main screen disables the mouse cancel (fields::Disable_Cancel_, mainscr_main.cpp:281), so the right button finds the map's grid field and Get_Input_ returns it NEGATIVE (fields.cpp:1360); Main_Screen_ then ends the relocation-merge mode and leaves zoom mode (mainscr_main.cpp:397-404). The star, ship and popup branches all want mouse_status 0 and a right click yields 1 (Get_Mouse_Field_, mainscr.cpp:1652), so no star, ship or popup branch runs - over a star, a black hole or empty space alike. One more thing does: on a zoomed-in map (_max_map_scale != _cur_map_scale) the same negative grid return scrolls the map to centre on the point clicked (Scroll_Map_, mainscr_main.cpp:858-863). HD sends CANCEL_FIELD on the grid field BEFORE its pan drag starts; the field is looked up in the live list by its type and rect (Add_Grid_Field_(22, 22, 1, 1, 506, 400), mainscr.cpp:1427, so x_end 527 and y_end 421) at the moment of the press (decision 20), and without it nothing is sent. A right click over a help region never gets here (decision 38).
map_cancel._deviation_scroll: DEVIATION map_cancel_scroll: the original's right-click scroll on a zoomed-in map is not HD's. HD's own zoom pans by the right-button drag; and CANCEL_FIELD right-clicks the grid field's CENTRE (orion2re's src/ext/ext_api.cpp, MSG_CANCEL_FIELD), so under the engine's own zoom Scroll_Map_ aims at the view's own middle, one native px off, and moves nothing (it moves only beyond 50, mainscr.cpp:2626). Behaviour unchanged by work order 310; registered in _markings.

_markings._note: The galaxy map's labelled departures that no other key here carries, each named as in the code; a smoke check (090zzzzm) holds this list and the code's labels both ways.
_markings.parallax: TRANSCRIPTION parallax (screens/galaxy_map/starfield.py parallax_offsets, StarfieldLayer.render): the star field in three layers moving 1x, 2x and 4x the map's scroll in world units, each tile drawn four times so it wraps, 0 at the widest scale (Draw_Paralax_ mainscr.cpp:650-680, Get_New_Paralax_XYs_ :2012-2059, Get_Map_Scale_ harold.cpp:1170-1178); the layers' shares measured off STARBG.LBX entries 0-2. Work order 310.
_markings.parallax_from_view: DEVIATION parallax_from_view (screens/galaxy_map/starfield.py parallax_offsets): the offset is read off the view's origin (-k x map_x), so the layers move against the scroll and a view always shows the same sky; the original adds each step's absolute size (mainscr.cpp:2020-2027), drifting right and down whichever way it scrolls. A zoom moves the layers by the same rule, HD's wheel zoom moving map_x; the original jumps them on a zoom instead (a zoom-out passes cur_map_x - old_x as the target, mainscr_main.cpp:838; leaving the zoom mode resets them to 0x16, :853-854), and only a scroll moves them by the scroll (mainscr.cpp:2521, :2634). The tile is the window, not 640 x 480 native px. Work order 310.
_markings.black_hole_order: TRANSCRIPTION black_hole_order (screens/galaxy_map/screen.py _render_map, renderer.render_stars black_holes=): the black holes in their own pass before the destination lines, the ETA line and the stars (Draw_Black_Holes_, mainscr_main.cpp:967-979). Work order 310.
_markings.names_over_stars: DEVIATION names_over_stars (screens/galaxy_map/screen.py _render_map): the star names after the stars, so over black holes and lines; the original prints them first (mainscr_main.cpp:949). HD's name sits inside its larger star sprite's lower part, which would cut it. Work order 310.
_markings.black_hole_turn: HD EXTENSION black_hole_turn (screens/galaxy_map/renderer.py BH_ROTATE_PERIOD_S): one master turned smoothly, 90 s a revolution; the original steps its sprite's frames, one every second draw (Draw_Black_Holes_ mainscr.cpp:729-737). Both stand still where Advance_Black_Hole_Animation_ says. Work order 310.
_markings.nebula_zoom3_hold: TRANSCRIPTION nebula_zoom3_hold (core/zoomtables.py NEBULA_HOLD_SCALE, nebula_native_dimension): past the scale of the original's rung the nebula keeps its size, as the original keeps the variant of its zoom level (mainscr.cpp:941-963): past 30 on an ordinary map (zoom 3, harold.cpp:1086-1110); on an extended one (over 72 stars) by Extended_Zoom_Level_For_Scale_ (map_scale.h:25-32), the zoom-2 size up to max_map_scale - 1 and the zoom-3 size only at the maximum. Work order 310.
_markings.system_window_blocks_map: DEVIATION system_window_blocks_map (screens/galaxy_map/boxdraw.py system_open): the original's star system window is moveable box 0 beside the map's own fields, and the grid field that hits stars and ships stays live around it (mainscr.cpp:1406, :1426; mainscr_main.cpp:421-438). HD blocks the whole map while it is open: Data's decision 5 of work order 226 F.
_markings.zoom_rocker: OMISSION zoom_rocker (screens/galaxy_map/viewctl.py): the original's ZOOM rocker, '+' at 244,428 and '-' at 244,455 with their own pictures (mainscr.cpp:1391-1392), is not drawn; HD zooms on the wheel and the + / - keys, and the engine's fields only park the game.
_markings.end_of_turn_stardate: TRANSCRIPTION end_of_turn_stardate (screens/galaxy_map/renderer.py): with end_of_turn_wait on, the original prints HESTR 0xDA and the stardate at (639, 0) in font 1 (mainscr_main.cpp:955-965) inside the map's clip window 22,22-527,421 (:952-953); the clipped printer drops text that ends above the window (fonts.cpp:190-197), so nothing shows, and HD draws nothing.
_markings.belt_hit: TRANSCRIPTION belt_hit (screens/galaxy_map/sysorbits.py belt_point; boxdraw.py belt_at, _inside): an asteroid belt has no planet field; the system window's grid field finds it by the orbit nearest the pointer from the scan centre (window corner + 171, + 134; Get_Orbit_From_X_Y_, geo.cpp:305-351; Scan_System_Display_Fields_, mainscr.cpp:2119-2163). Hovered it prints "Asteroids" without a highlight (sys.cpp:834-843); a click goes out as the native point in the grid field, and the engine answers an own outpost with box 217 (mainscr_main.cpp:567-577, mainscr.cpp:1567-1582). Work order 310.
_markings.drag_select: TRANSCRIPTION drag_select (screens/galaxy_map/boxpaint.py): the held left button paints the fleet box's cells with the value the press fixed - the opposite of the cell pressed, selected for a press beside the cells, nothing on the drag strip (mainscr_main.cpp:983-995, Set_Painted_Fleet_Fields_ mainscr.cpp:2468-2489, Icon_Selection_Status_ fleetpop.cpp:403-419); HD sends one MSG_SELECT_SHIP per newly painted cell it offers and nothing for a cell it does not offer, where the original paints every crossed cell and lets Ship_Can_Be_Selected_ refuse one (mainscr.cpp:2482, :2674); for the cells HD sends that gate still decides. The paint ends when its press is no longer held by HD's record (Mouse_Button_() == 1, mainscr_main.cpp:983) and on the screen's enter. Work order 310.
_markings.drag_strip_paint: OMISSION drag_strip_paint (screens/galaxy_map/boxpaint.py): in the original a press on the fleet box's drag strip still sets _mouse_btn_pressed, so a drag from the strip into the cells paints with the value the last gesture fixed (mainscr_main.cpp:986-993); HD's title stands on the strip and its press starts no paint. Work order 310.
_markings.box_cell_detail: OMISSION box_cell_detail (screens/galaxy_map/mapinput.py right_button): the original's right click on any cell of an own stack in the fleet box, offered for selection or not (Can_Select_Fleet_Box_Ship_, the owner only, mainscr.cpp:3319-3328), opens the ship's detailed view (Detailed_View_Ship_, mainscr.cpp:3428-3434); HD has no view and no wire block for it (parked, work order 200 P-B1), so the right click on such a cell does nothing and starts no pan. Work order 310.
_markings.star_click_radius: TRANSCRIPTION star_click_radius (screens/galaxy_map/screen.py _star_at): the first star in index order whose centre lies within Scaled_Star_Map_Dimension_({12, 10, 8}[star.size]) native px (Check_Stars_XY_, mainscr.cpp:1697-1740), in HD px of the view; until work order 310 HD took the nearest star within 0.6 x its drawn width (309's finding 4).
_markings.map_window_clip: TRANSCRIPTION map_window_clip (screens/galaxy_map/screen.py _render_map, _star_at): while HD mirrors the game, the map's objects are drawn inside the original's window 22,22-527,421 only (Draw_Main_Screen_, mainscr_main.cpp:939-940), and a click outside it hits no star: the side bands of a wider box lie past the game's slice (309's finding 11); inside it every star is tested, so one centred up to its radius past the edge is hit (Check_Stars_XY_, mainscr.cpp:1713-1739). The window is 506 x 400 native px, Set_Window_'s corners being inclusive (animate.cpp:105-107). The movable boxes are HD's and are not clipped; decoupled, the game is parked at full zoom-out and the whole box is map.
_markings.sidebar_windows: TRANSCRIPTION sidebar_windows (screens/galaxy_map/mapinput.py click): the Command and Freighters windows activate their own fields (command_window_field, freighters_window_field; mainscr_main.cpp:714-732): screen 43 or 35, which have no HD view and get the F12 notice, or the box HESTR 0xDF as MSGB; the food window has no handler and its click is swallowed (309's finding 2).
_markings.merge_relocation_marker: HD EXTENSION merge_relocation_marker (screens/galaxy_map/mergemark.py): while the engine's merge-relocation mode is on (F4, mainscr.cpp:3112-3129; MREL, open fix 102) and the pointer is over the map window, a target ring and the words labels.merge_relocation are drawn at the pointer, where the original swaps to its relocation cursor (:3120) and shows no words (309's finding 5).
_markings.influence_overlay: OMISSION influence_overlay (core/keyfwd.py WITHHELD_ALT): orion2re v2's influence view (Alt+V, v2 mainscr.cpp:1589, :1665-1666; Draw_Influence_Overlay :275-471), not in 1.60, is not drawn, and Alt+V is not passed on the galaxy map, so the key cannot change a mode HD does not show (309's finding 6).
_markings.zoom_mode_list: TRANSCRIPTION zoom_mode_list (screens/galaxy_map/mapmodal.py is_zoom_mode): the engine's own zoom mode's field list (Add_Map_Fields_, mainscr.cpp:1373-1383: '+', '-' and a hidden field over the whole screen, zoom_mode_field) is the map, not a modal HD has no view for, so no F12 notice stands over it (309's finding 14).
_markings.zoom_mode_exit: TRANSCRIPTION zoom_mode_exit (screens/galaxy_map/mapinput.py send_map_cancel): in the engine's own zoom mode a right click on the map sends CANCEL_FIELD to the whole-screen field (zoom_mode_field), the list having no grid field; the original leaves the mode on any negative input (Exit_Zooming_Mode_, mainscr_main.cpp:396-403; mainscr.cpp:1742-1748). Work order 310.
_markings.zoom_mode_picture: OMISSION zoom_mode_picture (screens/galaxy_map/mapmodal.py is_zoom_mode): the zoom mode's own picture, the map darkened under a zoom box that follows the pointer (_Darken_Fill_ and Draw_Main_Screen_For_Zooming_, mainscr_main.cpp:763-785, mainscr.cpp:3164), is not drawn; HD's map stands as it is until the mode ends. Work order 310.
_markings.orbit_slots: TRANSCRIPTION orbit_slots (screens/galaxy_map/ships.py orbit_slot_offset, _orbit_slot_pos): under HD's own zoom an icon in slot 0..4 is placed by Get_XYs_For_Orbiting_Ships_ at HD's rung, with the star's own size and the owner's sprite width, at the star the ship stands on (ships.cpp:289-326, :209, :222-252); a fresh order keeps its slot. Work order 310.
_markings.slot_five: DEVIATION slot_five (screens/galaxy_map/ships.py icon_screen_pos): a slot-5 ship not in transit is drawn centred on its own position; the original reads Get_Scaled_Value_(ship x/y) without the map's origin or the 21 px edge (ships.cpp:248-250). Work order 310.
_markings.monster_icon_dim: TRANSCRIPTION monster_icon_dim (core/zoomtables.py MONSTER_ICON_DIM, MONSTER_ICON_HEADER_DIM): a monster's HD icon is the box of the pixels its own sprite draws, per zoom, placed inside the sprite's header; the sprite is the one Get_Ship_Icon_Pict_Seg_ picks (ships.cpp:337-397), the headers and pixels read off BUFFER0.LBX 237-264. Work order 310.
_markings.monster_in_space: TRANSCRIPTION monster_in_space (screens/galaxy_map/ships.py icon_screen_pos): under HD's own zoom an Antaran or monster ship in transit has its sprite's corner at its point less half the player icon's header, BUFFER0.LBX 205 + zoom, and its drawn pixels at its own inset (Get_Ship_Icon_Coords_In_Space_, ships.cpp:514-531); a player's ship in transit stays centred on its box. Work order 310.
_markings.black_hole_draw: TRANSCRIPTION black_hole_draw (screens/galaxy_map/renderer.py render_stars; core/zoomtables.py black_hole_origin): the black hole placed by zoom_dist / 2 (mainscr.cpp:28, :706, :740), a frame wider than the header (a non-circular master's padded fallback) centred on that place; drawn at its sprite header 40/34/34/25, BLACK_HOLE_HEADER_DIM, DERIVED off BUFFER0.LBX 184-187 (decision 27). Work order 310.
_markings.strongest_ship_icon: HD EXTENSION strongest_ship_icon (screens/galaxy_map/shippics.py ShipPictures.icon, map_livery, ships._stack_picture): a player stack shows its representative ship's battle picture, facing right, cut to its visible pixels and fitted into the unchanged icon box, in the builder's shape (previous_owner's set) and the owner's colour; on the map that colour is laid at full strength over the whole plating whatever the livery's strength and pattern (its core kept), so each owner's stack reads in its colour as the tinted icon does; the map's own slot ship_pictures/<builder colour>_<picture>.png, then all_<picture>.png, first, the only picture for the colony, outpost and transport ships (45-47); held once per detail (painted_detail) and rescaled per box; the tinted master without a picture or with the setting map_ship_pictures off. The original draws one icon per owner colour (Get_Ship_Icon_Pict_Seg_, ships.cpp:336-397). Work order 311.
_markings.strongest_tie_by_cost: DEVIATION strongest_tie_by_cost (screens/galaxy_map/shippics.py strength): the player's own stack, rebuilt by Find_Ship_Stacks_' key (shipstak.cpp:72-75), is represented by the Avenger first, then the largest hull, then the higher design cost; the original sorts by size * 50 + picture_num (Build_Ship_Type_Array_, shipstak.cpp:283-316), so it breaks a size tie by picture_num and puts a Titan above the huge Avenger. Work order 311.
_markings.foreign_stack_head: DEVIATION foreign_stack_head (screens/galaxy_map/shippics.py ShipPictures.representative): a foreign stack shows the head the original sorted (its node_idx), not Data's strongest ship: rebuilding it from ships_raw would show undetected ships (Remove_Non_Detected_Ships_), and FSEL has no next_node (open fix 20 rev 3). Work order 311.

_sidebar_row_pad_note: Reference px between a sidebar row's text box and the separator above it (decision 71): dev:tools/hud_boxes.py writes the sb_*_text boxes this far inside their bands, and the screen draws each separator this far above its row's text. Ours, not measured.
_sidebar_icon_note: The readouts' icons are the HUD's glyphs (hudview); the PNG icons under assets/icons/ were loaded and never drawn and are gone since work order 269. POSITIONS ARE NOT HERE: every row owns two boxes in boxes.json, sb_<row>_text and sb_<row>_icon, both draggable and font-scalable in the F3 editor. sidebar_fonts are reference sizes multiplied by each text box's own font_scale. A text box style may carry "align": left | center | right. The icons are an HD addition; the original prints these five numbers over full-cell artwork.
_nebula_note: The twelve forms are the original STARBG.LBX nebula shapes (entry = type * 4 + zoom + 6, tools/nebula_extract.py); type_NN.png maps 1:1 to s_nebula.type NN, as _nebula_pict_seg[type % 12] does. SIZE DOES NOT COME FROM THE ARTWORK (decision 26): the master's width is the type's world footprint, core/zoomtables.py NEBULA_DIM column 0, through the current scale (nebula_native_dimension, HD EXTENSION: the original swaps four pre-drawn variants by zoom level, Draw_Nebulae_ mainscr.cpp:941-963, which never scales), held past the original's rung (TRANSCRIPTION nebula_zoom3_hold: 30 on an ordinary map, the extended ladder's own on a map over 72 stars); its height follows the master's aspect, anchored top-left. NEBULA_EXTENDED_SHRINK is settled False. The gas the game counts is the zoom-3 sprite's index > 5 (Point_Is_In_Nebula_N_, geo.cpp:119-138); dev:tools/nebula_overlay.py lays it over each master (work order 310).
_star_note: spectral_class 0..5 map to blue/white/yellow/orange/red/brown, class 6 is the black hole. star.size 0/1/2 is large/medium/small. Both confirmed in orion2_consts.h (STAR_CLASS) and used by renderer.CLASS_DIRS.
_sizing_note: Star and black hole sizes are NOT configured here. They come from core/zoomtables.py, transcribed from orion2re: MOX::_star_fields_dim {33,29,25,23,21,17} indexed by (zoom_level + star.size), and for the black hole its sprite header {40,34,34,25}, placed by Draw_Black_Holes_ zoom_dist {39,33,33,24} / 2; both ignore star.size. Changing them would desync HD from the original's proportions. The same holds for nebulas: NEBULA_DIM there holds the twelve types x four zoom variants read out of STARBG.LBX.

ship_icons._note: Ship and monster icons. Sizes are NOT configured here - they come from core/zoomtables.py (SHIP_ICON_DIM 11/10/9/8 px wide by zoom level, MONSTER_ICON_DIM per monster type and zoom level, the pixels the original's own sprite draws). Only zoom level changes an icon's size; galaxy size merely caps how far the player may zoom out, so a Small galaxy is stuck at zoom 0 and always draws the largest icon.
ship_icons._fit_note: How the HD artwork sits inside that native box, because the HD drawings do not share the original sprites' aspect ratios. 'height' (default) matches the original height - the dimension that decides whether a four-deep orbit stack collides, since slots sit only 11 - zoom px apart. 'width' matches the width and lets taller artwork overflow, which reads as an icon one size too big. 'box' never overflows. 'area' keeps the visual weight of the original box for artwork with a wildly different aspect - the eel master is 3.3:1 against the eel's native box (core/zoomtables.py MONSTER_ICON_DIM, 15 x 5 at zoom 0 and 5 x 4 at zoom 3), where width-fit and height-fit part furthest at the small steps.
ship_icons._kinds_note: Per-kind overrides of fit and scale; anything absent inherits the global value above. Keys are the asset folder names: player, antaran, guardian, amoeba, crystal, dragon, eel, hydra. 'scale' other than 1.0 is a deliberate departure from orion2re's footprint.
ship_icons._owner_note: Player colour needs the owner of each icon, which s_ship_icon does not carry. Open fix 20 sends the node table (_ship_node[].ship_idx per node) and the owner byte; ships.py reads them (resolve_owners) and does not rebuild the table from _ship[] (see its OWNER section). Run tools/ship_icon_check.py against a running game to see the resolved owner and sprite per icon.

home_ping._note: INVENTION, not a transcription: MOO2 has no home-system ping and cannot alpha-blend at all. A navigation aid for large galaxies at HD resolutions. The key is consumed by OrionLayer and never forwarded to orion2re, so it takes nothing away from the game; HOME is chosen because the original binds no such key on the galaxy map. Timing and radii live in screens/galaxy_map/ping.py.

movable_boxes._note: The system window and the fleet box, drawn by HD (brief 110 Part A step 2, screens/galaxy_map/boxdraw.py and boxmodel.py). Every other word in them is the original's, from HESTRNGS. The buttons' labels are the words the original draws as artwork (CLOSE, and since work order 229 ALL and the order buttons, screens/galaxy_map/fleetorders.py), so they live here (decision 15). The boxes are system_* and fleet_* in boxes.json; a box sits on the side of the map the game's own window is on.

research_window_field._source: MAINSCR: _research_window_field = Add_Hidden_Field_(545, 344, 613, 415, "", 0x29) (mainscr.cpp:1405) - the LAST of the five sidebar windows; four of the five have a handler (the food window none): mainscr_main.cpp:697-713 sets _return_screen = SCREEN_MAIN and _current_screen = SCREEN_TECH_CHANGE, and Screen_Control_ then calls TECH::Tech_Change_ (mox2.cpp:177-180). The handler COMPARES THE ID (:697, guarded by _skip_fields == 0), so ACTIVATE_FIELD reaches it - unlike a radio button, which is resolved through the pointer. Looked up in the LIVE list by type and rect and never by a remembered index (decision 20), the way parking looks up its own two fields: a list without this field is not the galaxy map's, whatever the game reports.

system_stars._note: The star system window's stars (work order 230 C, screens/galaxy_map/sysstars.py): one point per native_px_per_star native px of the window, at the measured colours of BUFFER0.LBX 0x49; seed lays them out. A mod may change both, or ship screens/galaxy_map/assets/system_stars.png to replace the points.

treasury_window_field._source: MAINSCR: _treasury_window_field = Add_Hidden_Field_(545, 49, 613, 119, "", 0x29) (mainscr.cpp:1401) - the sidebar's first window; its handler clears the map's fields and runs Tax_Rate_Popup_ (mainscr_main.cpp:733-748). The handler compares the id, so ACTIVATE_FIELD reaches it. Looked up in the LIVE list by type and rect (decision 20), as research_window_field. Work order 230 D.

command_window_field._source: MAINSCR: _command_points_window_field = Add_Hidden_Field_(545, 122, 613, 192, "", 0x29) (mainscr.cpp:1402) - the sidebar's second window; its handler compares the id and, under _skip_fields == 0, sets _return_screen = SCREEN_MAIN and _current_screen = 43, SCREEN_SHOW_COMMAND_POINTS (mainscr_main.cpp:727-732; v2 :735-739). HD has no view of that screen: the F12 notice names it (core/screen_names.py). Looked up in the LIVE list by type and rect (decision 20), as treasury_window_field. Work order 310.

freighters_window_field._source: MAINSCR: _freighters_window_field = Add_Hidden_Field_(545, 270, 613, 340, "", 0x29) (mainscr.cpp:1404) - the sidebar's fourth window; its handler compares the id: with no freighter (_player[].n_freighters < 1) the box HESTR 0xDF, which comes as MSGB, else _current_screen = 35, SCREEN_SCRAP_FREIGHTERS (mainscr_main.cpp:714-726; v2 :724-734). HD has no view of that screen: the F12 notice names it (core/screen_names.py). Looked up in the LIVE list by type and rect (decision 20). Work order 310.

zoom_mode_field._source: MAINSCR: in the engine's own zoom mode (_zoom_in == 1) Add_Map_Fields_ clears the map's fields and adds only '+', '-' and _whole_screen_field = Add_Hidden_Field_(0, 0, 639, 479, "", 0x29) (mainscr.cpp:1373-1383; v2 :1537-1547): no grid field, so the map's own test (map_cancel and zoom_out_field) fails. This field with zoom_out_field is the zoom mode's list, which the map's modal net counts as the map (screens/galaxy_map/mapmodal.py is_zoom_mode), not as a modal HD has no view for (309's finding 14). Work order 310.

tax_rate._note: The tax rate popup's words (work order 230 D, screens/galaxy_map/taxrate.py): the original's popup, rate buttons and ACCEPT are TAXRATE artwork with no string (mainpups.cpp:207-237) - typed here per decision 15. The title is the original picture's words, read off the native frame (work order 230).
tax_rate.title: Set Tax Rate
